texto.es: Para ahorrar espacio, los titulares omiten artículos y el verbo be. Usan el presente para hechos ya ocurridos (Councillors vote = votaron), to + verbo para el futuro (School strike to start = empezará) y el participio para la pasiva sin be (Pool closed = se ha cerrado). Para expandir un titular: 1) añade the/a, 2) recupera el auxiliar, 3) elige el tiempo correcto. También abundan las formas impersonales (is expected to, reportedly), que dan el dato sin nombrar la fuente, y las palabras cortas como hike, probe, bid, pledge, halt, unveil, slash o plunge, que condensan una acción entera.

texto.es: Dos noticias pueden contar el mismo hecho y diferir en tres cosas. La fuente: ¿quién lo dice? (un spokesperson oficial, un eyewitness, una fuente anonymous, nadie). La certeza: said o confirmed son firmes; claims o allegedly dejan la duda; insist y admit ya interpretan lo dicho. Y las palabras valorativas (chaos, shocking), que son opinión y no pueden comprobarse, a diferencia de los hechos (a las ocho, 300 personas). Una noticia credible da pruebas de cada afirmación. Para comparar dos noticias, sepáralo todo en una tabla: hecho, fuente, certeza y valoración, y marca cada discrepancy entre ellas.

nota.es: fuente oficial y verbo firme: dato fiable
testigo y verbo que deja la duda
allegedly: se afirma, sin pruebas
palabra valorativa: opinión, no hecho

titulo.es: La noticia breve: pirámide, fuentes y cautela

texto.es: Una noticia breve va de lo más importante a lo menos: titular, lead (qué pasó, cuánto, cuándo, dónde) y detalles. Cada dato importante lleva su fuente: said, according to, told. El grado de certeza se marca con el verbo y con formas impersonales (is expected to, is believed to) y con palabras como provisional cuando la cifra no está cerrada. El tono es impartial: sin chaos ni amazing; las opiniones van entre comillas y atribuidas (said one pupil), y cuando no citas textualmente haces una paraphrase sin comillas. Con dos fuentes distintas, por ejemplo la organizadora y la directora, la noticia resulta equilibrada.

I would rewrite it as: apparently, the centre may close in July, but there is no proof yet. Second, the council has already signed the papers comes from a cleaner who told someone's cousin, which is hearsay, so I would write that, according to an unverified account, the council may have signed them. texto.es: Para comprobar un texto, busca afirmaciones sin fuente: frases con everyone knows, obviously o clearly, sweeping claims y datos sin nombre ni documento (un rumour, hearsay). Reescríbelas con dos movimientos. 1) Atribuir: according to the letter, the director said. 2) Ajustar la certeza (hedge): apparently, may, these numbers suggest. Si no hay ninguna fuente, no inventes: escribe que está unverified o que there is no proof yet. Si una afirmación resulta falsa, retract y debunk: se retira y se desmonta con datos. Después justifica el cambio: «añadí la fuente» o «bajé la certeza», porque un buen chequeo explica qué se cambió y por qué.

items.respuesta: I found three doubtful claims in the post. First, the sports centre will close in July is presented as a fact, but no source is named, so it is only a rumour. I would rewrite it as: apparently, the centre may close in July, but there is no proof yet. Second, the council has already signed the papers comes from a cleaner who told someone's cousin, which is hearsay, so I would write that, according to an unverified account, the council may have signed them. Third, the new rule is clearly unfair is a sweeping claim that uses an opinion word, and I would change it to: some members suggest that the rule may be unfair. I made these changes because every claim needs a source, and because cautious words such as apparently and may show what we do not know yet. titulo.es: Quién cuenta, cuánto sabe y con qué actitud

texto.es: La voz narrativa responde a tres preguntas: ¿quién cuenta?, ¿cuánto sabe? y ¿con qué actitud? En primera persona (I, my) el narrador es un personaje y solo conoce lo que vive. En tercera persona limitada (she, Mara) seguimos la mente de un solo personaje. En la omnisciente, el narrador está al tanto de varias mentes y puede comentar desde fuera. Un narrador en primera persona puede ser poco fiable, y el tono puede ser cálido o distante. Con she no basta: cuenta las mentes y busca pistas.

Free indirect style lets a narrator slip into a character's head without warning: Mara looked at the clock, and then came the question, was he really going to be late again?
He would surely come tomorrow. Of course he would! The narrator never writes that she thought it, yet her certainty comes through clearly.
What a silly idea this was! The exclamation and the word this are subtle signals of her reaction, more direct than any reporting verb such as thought or wondered.

Mara felt nervous, and her mind went back to that day. Was it really her fault? The shift from narration to question is almost invisible.
Free indirect style can blur the line between narrator and character, so you must decide whose thoughts you are reading before you attribute an opinion to either.

titulo.es: Narrador y personaje en la misma frase

texto.es: El estilo indirecto libre mezcla la voz del narrador con la del personaje. Sigue en tercera persona y en pasado, pero sin verbos como she thought o she said. Se reconoce por rasgos de la voz directa: preguntas directas, con su inversión (Was he late?), exclamaciones (What a silly idea!), adverbios del momento del personaje (now, tomorrow) y palabras como surely. Compara: Mara thought that he would be late es indirecto; He would be late again! es libre. Pregúntate siempre: ¿quién habla aquí, el narrador o el personaje?

exclamación: voz del personaje
tomorrow con would: mirada del personaje

filas.texto: Mara thought that he would be late.

items.texto: Free indirect style lets a narrator slip into a character's head without warning: Mara looked at the clock, and then came the question, was he really going to be late again?

traduccion.es: El estilo indirecto libre permite que el narrador se deslice hacia la cabeza del personaje sin aviso: Mara miró el reloj y entonces llegó la pregunta: ¿de verdad iba a llegar tarde otra vez?

nota.es: La pregunta directa dentro de la narración en pasado es la voz de Mara: no hay «she asked herself».

items.texto: He would surely come tomorrow. Of course he would! The narrator never writes that she thought it, yet her certainty comes through clearly.

traduccion.es: Seguro que vendría mañana. ¡Claro que vendría! El narrador nunca escribe que ella lo pensó, pero su certeza se oye con claridad.

nota.es: Tomorrow en un relato en pasado es marca de estilo libre: el narrador diría the next day.

items.texto: What a silly idea this was! The exclamation and the word this are subtle signals of her reaction, more direct than any reporting verb such as thought or wondered.

traduccion.es: ¡Qué idea tan tonta era esta! La exclamación y la palabra this son señales sutiles de su reacción, más directas que cualquier verbo de transmisión como thought o wondered.

nota.es: What a + exclamación es la voz de ella; this (y no that) acerca el texto a su mente; reporting verb = said, thought, wondered…

items.texto: She had no doubt about it: he was coming, and nothing could stop him now. The word now belongs to her present, not to the narrator's past.

traduccion.es: No tenía ninguna duda: él venía y nada podía detenerlo ahora. La palabra now pertenece al presente de ella, no al pasado del narrador.

nota.es: Now dentro de un relato en pasado muestra el punto de vista del personaje, no el del narrador.

items.texto: Mara felt nervous, and her mind went back to that day. Was it really her fault? The shift from narration to question is almost invisible.

traduccion.es: Mara se sentía nerviosa y su mente volvió a aquel día. ¿De verdad era culpa suya? El paso de la narración a la pregunta casi no se nota.

nota.es: Primero narración (felt nervous) y luego pensamiento en forma de pregunta directa, en pasado.

items.texto: Free indirect style can blur the line between narrator and character, so you must decide whose thoughts you are reading before you attribute an opinion to either.

traduccion.es: El estilo indirecto libre puede difuminar la frontera entre narrador y personaje, así que debes decidir de quién son los pensamientos antes de atribuir una opinión a uno u otro.

nota.es: Blur = difuminar: cuando no se separan las voces, pregúntate quién habla.

titulo.es: Del gesto al ánimo y al motivo

texto.es: En un cuento, el ánimo del personaje casi nunca se dice con una sola palabra: se deduce de lo que hace y de cómo se cuenta. Fíjate en tres cosas. 1) Los adjetivos de ánimo (anxious, relieved, guilty, reluctant). 2) Las acciones que lo muestran (hesitate, avoid, stare). 3) El motivo: ¿por qué actúa así? Al responder una pregunta de comprensión, cita la pista del texto en vez de adivinar. Una expresión clave puede tener sentido literal y emocional: elige el que encaja con la escena.
Ánimo + acción + motivo:

nota.es: adjetivo de ánimo
acción que lo muestra
motivo: la causa

items.texto: Mara feels anxious before the exam, so she tries to avoid her friends, and by the evening she has come to dread every conversation about results.

traduccion.es: Mara se siente inquieta antes del examen, así que intenta evitar a sus amigos, y por la tarde ya teme cualquier conversación sobre las notas.

nota.es: El ánimo (anxious) explica la acción (avoid) y dread nombra el miedo a lo que viene: del motivo a la conducta.

items.texto: Leo is eager to start the project, but his sister looks reluctant, probably because she cannot forget how badly the last one ended.

traduccion.es: Leo tiene muchas ganas de empezar el proyecto, pero su hermana parece reacia, probablemente porque no olvida lo mal que acabó el último.

nota.es: Eager y reluctant son opuestos: muchas ganas frente a poca gana de hacer algo, y el texto suele dar la razón.

items.texto: When the door finally opened, Tom felt relieved: nobody had seen him, and he could brush off the teasing that would certainly follow.

traduccion.es: Cuando por fin se abrió la puerta, Tom se sintió aliviado: nadie lo había visto y podría quitar importancia a las burlas que seguramente vendrían.

nota.es: Relieved es el ánimo de quien deja de preocuparse; had seen sitúa el hecho antes del alivio y brush off es restar importancia.

items.texto: She felt guilty because she had not called her grandmother, and the longer she waited, the more sheepish she felt about picking up the phone.

traduccion.es: Se sentía culpable porque no había llamado a su abuela, y cuanto más esperaba, más cohibida se sentía para contestar el teléfono.

nota.es: Guilty + because da el motivo de la emoción con un hecho anterior (had not called); sheepish añade vergüenza.

items.texto: He began to hesitate at the door, and his real motive, which he never admitted to anyone, was to say sorry.

traduccion.es: Empezó a dudar ante la puerta, y su verdadero motivo, que nunca admitió ante nadie, era pedir perdón.

nota.es: Hesitate es una acción que muestra el ánimo; motive es la razón que explica lo que hace.

items.texto: She did not speak; she only continued to stare at the old photo, and that silence told the reader more than any adjective could have done.

traduccion.es: No habló; solo siguió mirando fijamente la vieja foto, y ese silencio dijo al lector más de lo que habría dicho cualquier adjetivo.

nota.es: Stare at es una acción sin palabras: el autor muestra el ánimo sin nombrarlo.

consigna.es: Lee el texto. ¿Qué explica mejor la conducta de Mara?

feedback.es: Evitar a los amigos y contestar con una palabra sugiere inquietud ante algo que no quiere tratar, no ganas de estar sola.

pista.es: Fíjate en las acciones: ¿qué ánimo y qué motivo encajan con ellas?

I remember standing on my grandmother's porch on hot summer evenings, when the air was warm and heavy and the scent of fresh bread drifted out of the kitchen. I can still hear the creak of the old gate and the echo of my cousins laughing in the garden. I will never forget watching the sun go down behind the hills while she told us stories about her own childhood. One evening I forgot to say goodbye when my parents took me home, and I still regret not hugging her that night. When I look back on those summers, I realise how much they shaped me. Now I must remember to call her every Sunday, because the scent of bread alone is not enough to keep a voice alive. Some memories linger for ever, small and golden, exactly as they were.

titulo.es: Verbos de memoria: -ing para recordar, to para no olvidar

texto.es: Algunos verbos cambian de significado según lo que sigue. Remember y forget + -ing hablan de un recuerdo de algo que ya ocurrió (I remember playing…, I will never forget hearing…). Remember y forget + to hablan de una tarea (I must remember to call; I forgot to lock the door). Regret + -ing lamenta algo hecho o no hecho (I regret not saying goodbye). En una escena de recuerdo, cuenta en primera persona, añade detalles de los sentidos (scent, creak, warm) y usa estos verbos para pasar del ahora al antes.
Verbo de memoria + -ing (recuerdo) o to (tarea):

nota.es: remember + -ing: recuerdo de algo vivido
remember + to: no olvidar hacer algo
regret + -ing: lamento lo que hice o no hice

nota.es: Remember + to es no olvidar una tarea futura; forgot to + verbo indica que no hiciste algo por olvido.

items.texto: I regret not saying goodbye to her properly, and when I look back on that evening, I wish I had stayed a little longer.

nota.es: Regret + -ing lamenta algo que hiciste o no hiciste; not va delante del -ing; look back on = recordar un periodo pasado.

items.texto: The scent of warm bread used to linger in the hallway, and it is still the most vivid memory I have of that house.

items.texto: An echo of her voice still stays in my mind, which shows how a single detail can bring back an entire scene.

pista.es: Un recuerdo de algo vivido lleva el verbo de memoria seguido de -ing.

items.respuesta: I remember standing on my grandmother's porch on hot summer evenings, when the air was warm and heavy and the scent of fresh bread drifted out of the kitchen. I can still hear the creak of the old gate and the echo of my cousins laughing in the garden. I will never forget watching the sun go down behind the hills while she told us stories about her own childhood. One evening I forgot to say goodbye when my parents took me home, and I still regret not hugging her that night. When I look back on those summers, I realise how much they shaped me. Now I must remember to call her every Sunday, because the scent of bread alone is not enough to keep a voice alive. Some memories linger for ever, small and golden, exactly as they were.

It is a vivid memory, and I do not want to forget it.

texto.es: En un club de lectura haces tres cosas. Primero resumes lo que pasa (In this chapter, the plot turns when…), para que todos sepan de qué hablas. Después conectas con tu experiencia: I can relate to…, It reminds me of…, I remember + -ing. Por último respondes a otra opinión con tacto: I see your point, but I disagree, o usas although para contrastar. Da siempre un motivo a tu valoración (moving, gripping) y cierra con una pregunta para mantener abierta la conversación.

items.respuesta: Thanks, Tom. I see your point, but I would take issue with the claim that the ending was rushed. In chapter six, the plot turns when Mara finds her grandmother's old letter hidden in an old book, and the pacing slows so that we can feel her hesitation. Although the final pages are quiet, I found them very moving. I can relate to Mara, because I remember waiting for a letter from my own grandmother every summer. I will never forget opening the envelope and seeing her small, careful handwriting. That memory made the last scene feel true to me, and it is bound to strike a chord with anyone who has waited for news. Perhaps the ending is not exciting, but it is honest. I also regret not keeping her letters, which may be why the chapter reminds me of her so strongly. What do the rest of you think?

texto.es: En un debate de nivel C1, conceder un punto no es perder: reconoces lo que tiene de cierto la otra postura y enseguida vuelves a tu conclusión. Granted y admittedly van al principio de la frase, con coma, y la réplica llega después, normalmente con but. Be that as it may, that said y even so abren la réplica por sí solos, sin but. titulo.es: Consecuencia y medio en registro formal

texto.es: En un texto formal hay cuatro conectores para hablar de consecuencia y medio. Hence («de ahí») va con un nombre o una oración: hence the drop in traffic. Thereby + -ing indica lo que se consigue con la acción anterior: thereby reducing traffic. Whereby (= by which) presenta un sistema o una regla: a scheme whereby residents pay less. In so doing empieza frase nueva y retoma la acción anterior: «al hacerlo». Son conectores de escritura; al hablar dirías so o by doing this.
Acción + thereby + -ing:

nota.es: la acción o decisión
con lo cual: une acción y resultado
verbo en -ing: la consecuencia

filas.texto: a scheme whereby residents pay less
In so doing, the council won support.

items.texto: The council introduced a fee for private cars; hence the sharp drop in traffic, which surprised even its most committed critics.

traduccion.es: El municipio introdujo una tarifa para los autos particulares; de ahí el fuerte descenso del tráfico, que sorprendió incluso a sus críticos más convencidos.

nota.es: Hence + nombre (o una oración) da la consecuencia; es formal y se usa al escribir.

items.texto: The council charges a fee to discourage drivers, thereby reducing traffic and, in turn, improving the air that residents breathe.

traduccion.es: El municipio cobra una tarifa para desalentar a los conductores, con lo cual reduce el tráfico y, a su vez, mejora el aire que respiran los residentes.

nota.es: Thereby + verbo en -ing expresa el resultado de la acción anterior; in turn enlaza un resultado con el siguiente.

items.texto: The council created a scheme whereby residents pay only half the fee, provided that they can prove they live inside the zone.

traduccion.es: El municipio creó un plan por el cual los residentes pagan solo la mitad de la tarifa, siempre que puedan demostrar que viven dentro de la zona.

nota.es: Whereby (= by which) presenta el sistema o la regla con la que algo funciona.

items.texto: The council lowered the fee for residents. In so doing, it won their support and helped to curb the opposition that had formed.

traduccion.es: El municipio bajó la tarifa para los residentes. Al hacerlo, ganó su apoyo y ayudó a frenar la oposición que se había formado.

nota.es: In so doing retoma la acción anterior y da su resultado; el sujeto es el mismo. Curb = frenar.

items.texto: The levy is cheap to run and easy to explain, hence its popularity among officials who need results before the next election.

traduccion.es: La tasa es barata de gestionar y fácil de explicar; de ahí su popularidad entre los funcionarios que necesitan resultados antes de las próximas elecciones.

nota.es: Hence puede ir delante de un nombre sin verbo: hence its popularity. Levy es una tasa impuesta por una autoridad.

items.texto: The fee pays for new buses, thereby helping commuters, and it gives drivers a genuine incentive to leave their cars at home.

nota.es: Thereby helping: la ayuda es la consecuencia directa de pagar los autobuses; incentive es lo que motiva un cambio.

titulo.es: El mapa de un debate: cuatro piezas

texto.es: Para seguir un debate de dos voces, construye un mapa con cuatro piezas. El argumento es la postura de alguien con su razón: My main argument is… El contraargumento es la respuesta del otro lado: On the other hand…, But… La concesión es lo que alguien admite: Granted…, Admittedly… El cierre resume: To sum up… Escucha primero quién está a favor y quién en contra y luego ubica cada pieza por su palabra señal. El mapa recoge lo que dicen ellos, no tu opinión.
Mapa del debate:

nota.es: argumento: postura y razón
concesión y contraargumento
cierre: resumen final

items.texto: The moderator reads the motion aloud and gives each speaker two minutes, then reminds the audience to weigh up the arguments before voting.

traduccion.es: La moderadora lee la moción en voz alta y da dos minutos a cada orador; luego recuerda al público que sopese los argumentos antes de votar.

nota.es: El moderador dirige el debate; la moción es la frase que se discute; weigh up = sopesar.

items.texto: The motion is that mobile phones should be banned in class, and Tom is in favour of it, although his stance is more nuanced than it sounds.

nota.es: In favour of = a favor de; stance es la postura que alguien defiende.

items.texto: Ana is against the motion, and her main contention is that phones are useful tools, provided that teachers set clear limits.

traduccion.es: Ana está en contra de la moción y su tesis principal es que los teléfonos son herramientas útiles, siempre que los profesores pongan límites claros.

nota.es: Against va sin preposición detrás: against the motion; contention es la tesis que alguien defiende con sus razones.

items.texto: Tom's counterargument is that the premise behind Ana's case, that students use phones only for study, is simply unrealistic.

traduccion.es: El contraargumento de Tom es que la premisa del caso de Ana, que los estudiantes usan el teléfono solo para estudiar, es sencillamente poco realista.

nota.es: El contraargumento responde a lo que dijo el otro orador; la premisa es la idea que se da por supuesta.

items.texto: Both speakers eventually find some common ground, yet each expects the other to carry the burden of proof, and their closing statements still differ on whether a total ban is necessary.

traduccion.es: Ambos oradores acaban encontrando cierto terreno común, pero cada uno espera que el otro cargue con la carga de la prueba, y sus declaraciones de cierre siguen difiriendo sobre si hace falta una prohibición total.

nota.es: Common ground = lo que ambos aceptan; burden of proof = quién debe demostrar su tesis; closing statement: la frase final donde cada orador resume su postura.

traduccion.es: En resumen, el debate demuestra que la moción divide a la clase, y un buen moderador recoge cada argumento con justicia.

Nonetheless, a later start would mean finishing classes after five, so pupils would lose time for sport and for homework. Dear editor, thank you for your letter. I take your point about sleep, and I would not deny that many teenagers arrive at school tired. Nonetheless, the evidence you quote comes from a single school, so the claim does not hold up. With respect, a later start would also end the day after five, which would leave little time for sport, homework or part-time work. While the idea has some merit, it would be hard for parents who start work early and for the buses that bring pupils to school. To rebut your main argument, look at the schools that already use a new timetable: most pupils adapt within a few weeks, and their results barely change. On the contrary, it would be unfair to overstate the problem. I therefore hope that the council will think again before it changes anything. Yours faithfully, Ana

Polite but firm: she questions the evidence without attacking the person.

I see where you are coming from, and I would not deny that a later start suits some pupils. While that may be true, the study you mention has not been repeated elsewhere. With respect, one school is not enough to rewrite an entire timetable.

titulo.es: Conceder con cortesía y rebatir con evidencia

texto.es: Una buena réplica escrita hace dos movimientos por cada punto: concede y rebate. Concedes con I take your point (about…), I would not deny that… o While + oración: While later lessons could help sleep,… Rebates con nonetheless, but o con evidencia: the evidence suggests… Para mantener la cortesía usa with respect y ataca la idea, no a la persona. Estructura recomendada: apertura, concesión 1 y contraargumento 1, concesión 2 y contraargumento 2, y cierre.
Concesión + nonetheless + contraargumento:

formula.texto: I would not deny that teenagers are tired.

nota.es: concesión: admites un punto cierto
giro: «aun así»

nota.es: contraargumento con datos

nota.es: I take your point concede con cortesía antes de rebatir; evidence = pruebas, datos.

traduccion.es: No negaría que los adolescentes están cansados; aun así, empezar más tarde causaría serios problemas a los padres que trabajan.

nota.es: I would not deny that + oración concede; nonetheless abre la réplica.

items.texto: While a later start could help pupils sleep, it would also end the school day later and shorten their free afternoons.

traduccion.es: Si bien empezar más tarde podría ayudar a los alumnos a dormir, también haría que el día terminara más tarde y acortaría sus tardes libres.

nota.es: While + concesión, coma y réplica: no se añade but.

items.texto: With respect, the evidence you quote comes from only one school, so the claim does not really hold up.

traduccion.es: Con el debido respeto, las pruebas que citas vienen de un solo colegio, así que la afirmación no se sostiene del todo.

nota.es: With respect suaviza el desacuerdo antes de una crítica; hold up = resistir el análisis.

items.texto: To rebut this claim, look at the schools that already use a new timetable, where there is little merit in the complaints.

traduccion.es: Para rebatir esta afirmación, mira los colegios que ya usan un horario nuevo, donde las quejas tienen poco fundamento.

nota.es: To rebut = para rebatir: respondes a una afirmación con datos; merit = valor, fundamento.

items.texto: It would be unfair to overstate the problem, and on the contrary, the data suggest that most pupils adapt within weeks.

traduccion.es: Sería injusto exagerar el problema y, al contrario, los datos sugieren que la mayoría de los alumnos se adaptan en semanas.

nota.es: Overstate = exagerar; on the contrary corrige una idea con la postura opuesta.

consigna.es: Elige la réplica que concede el punto y lo rebate con cortesía.

feedback.es: Concede el punto del sueño y lo rebate con un problema concreto; las otras dos atacan sin conceder o repiten la tesis ajena.

pista.es: Busca la réplica que concede algo y después aporta un contraargumento nuevo.

items.respuesta: Dear editor, thank you for your letter. I take your point about sleep, and I would not deny that many teenagers arrive at school tired. Nonetheless, the evidence you quote comes from a single school, so the claim does not hold up. With respect, a later start would also end the day after five, which would leave little time for sport, homework or part-time work. While the idea has some merit, it would be hard for parents who start work early and for the buses that bring pupils to school. To rebut your main argument, look at the schools that already use a new timetable: most pupils adapt within a few weeks, and their results barely change. On the contrary, it would be unfair to overstate the problem. I therefore hope that the council will think again before it changes anything. Yours faithfully, Ana

Nonetheless, the evidence in your letter comes from only one school, and with respect, that does not prove very much. While a later start could help some teenagers, it would also end the day after five, so pupils would lose time for sport, for homework and for work. Thank you, chair. My position is clear: the city centre should be closed to cars at weekends. Granted, congestion is a real problem, and some shops fear that they will lose customers. Nonetheless, the evidence from other cities suggests that pedestrian streets bring more visitors, thereby helping shops rather than harming them. Hence the growing support among parents, who want safer streets for their children. With respect, my opponent says that free buses would be a better solution, but that plan would cost too much and may not prove viable. Admittedly, a car-free centre involves a trade-off, yet on balance the benefits outweigh the costs. A scheme whereby residents keep access to their homes would protect the people who live here. In so doing, the council would show that it listens to both sides. To sum up, we should tackle traffic now, before urban life becomes impossible. Thank you.

texto.es: En un panel cada turno tiene un trabajo. La apertura da tu postura en una frase y dos o tres razones (My position is clear…). La concesión admite un punto cierto del otro lado (Granted…, Admittedly…, I take your point…). La refutación responde con evidencia y un conector formal (Nonetheless,…; hence…; thereby + -ing; a scheme whereby…). El cierre sintetiza con On balance… o To sum up… Usa los cuatro movimientos y mantén la cortesía con With respect…

Thank you, chair. I am against a full ban on cars in the centre, and I would like to explain why. To be fair, my opponent is right that congestion is a problem, and I would not deny that pedestrian streets are safer. That said, the evidence from our own city shows that shops lost much of their takings when a nearby street closed. Hence the concern of traders, who cannot wait for years to see whether visitors return. Even so, I am willing to concede that some streets could close, thereby giving families more space. A scheme whereby residents and traders vote street by street would be more viable than a single decision for the whole centre. With respect, a trade-off that ignores the people who work here is not a fair one. On balance, I believe that we should test one street first and tackle congestion step by step. Thank you.

titulo.es: Las jugadas de un hilo de reclamación

texto.es: Un hilo de reclamación avanza por «jugadas», y cada una transmite una actitud distinta. Chase recuerda con paciencia algo pendiente; escalate sube el asunto a alguien con más autoridad y suena más duro, por eso llega después de un recordatorio; acknowledge pide o da confirmación de que el mensaje llegó; close the loop avisa del resultado final. En C1 importa lo que el remitente da a entender: «as a gentle reminder» es paciente; «I will have no choice but to…» anuncia una consecuencia.

el dato concreto que falta

titulo.es: Firme no es lo mismo que brusco

texto.es: Una frase seca («Answer me now») se arregla sin perder firmeza: mantén los dos datos duros, qué quieres y para cuándo, y cambia el envoltorio. Suaviza con just, kindly o I am afraid; pide con I would be grateful if you could…; repite la petición con reiterate y cierra con I look forward to hearing from you. Repasa también el causativo: have + objeto + participio («have the heater repaired») pide que lo haga otra persona; repair solo dice que lo haces tú.

texto.es: Para entender una cadena de correos busca tres cosas: el problema (qué falla y desde cuándo), el plazo (una visita, un límite del cliente o un tiempo de espera) y la solución acordada (quién hace qué y cuándo; suele ir tras As agreed…). Los datos cambian de un correo a otro y manda el último. Vigila las palabras que corrigen lo anterior (but, however, too long) y lo que un correo da a entender sin decirlo: un gesto de cortesía no es una admisión de culpa, y un plazo no es una solución.

titulo.es: Un reclamo firme y cortés en cinco partes

texto.es: Un correo de reclamo a una empresa que ya no respondió una vez tiene cinco partes. 1) Referencia: recuerda tu correo anterior con fecha. 2) Problema: hechos y fechas, sin insultos (unacceptable califica la situación, no a las personas). 3) Petición y plazo: una acción concreta con fecha, apoyada si puedes en un derecho (I am entitled to…). 4) Consecuencia: el siguiente paso, con cortesía (Failing that…). 5) Cierre: confías en una respuesta pronta y pides una garantía (I trust that…).

nota.es: referencia: recuerdas el primer correo

petición y plazo

nota.es: El problema va con un hecho y una fecha. Unacceptable es firme pero no insulta; particularly as explica por qué importa.

nota.es: La disculpa suaviza, pero but + be entitled to apoya la petición con un derecho. Resolve + objeto = dar solución.

titulo.es: Del correo de la empresa al acuerdo

texto.es: Un caso de servicio completo junta tres movimientos. Primero, entender la respuesta: qué ofrece la empresa y con qué límites (parcial no es total). Segundo, redactar tu petición final: qué pides y para cuándo. Tercero, gestionar la contraoferta: aceptar (I am happy to accept…), rechazar con cortesía (I am afraid I must decline…) o negociar (I am willing to settle for… on the condition that…; Could we meet halfway?). Suaviza el tono, nunca el plazo, y deja constancia de que actúas de buena fe.

items.texto: The company has sent a counteroffer: a partial refund instead of a full one, which leaves the customer very little leeway.

traduccion.es: La empresa ha enviado una contraoferta: un reembolso parcial en lugar de uno total, lo que deja muy poco margen de maniobra a la clienta.

nota.es: Partial no es total: lee con qué límites ofrece la empresa. Leeway es el margen que queda para moverse.

items.texto: I am afraid I must decline the offer as it stands, but I am writing in good faith, and I would like to negotiate.

traduccion.es: Me temo que debo rechazar la oferta tal como está, pero escribo de buena fe y me gustaría negociar.

nota.es: Decline rechaza con cortesía; in good faith muestra que no buscas el conflicto; negotiate abre la puerta a un acuerdo.

items.texto: I am willing to settle for a partial refund, on the condition that you repair the machine by the end of the month.

traduccion.es: Estoy dispuesto a conformarme con un reembolso parcial, con la condición de que repare la máquina antes de que acabe el mes.

nota.es: Settle for + algo: aceptas menos de lo pedido. On the condition that va seguido de oración completa (sujeto + verbo).

items.texto: To reach a compromise, I can meet you halfway: I will accept half the price now if the rest follows within six weeks.

traduccion.es: Para llegar a un acuerdo a medias, puedo ceder la mitad: aceptaré la mitad del precio ahora si el resto llega en seis semanas.

nota.es: Meet you halfway propone un punto medio; el compromise exige que ambas partes cedan algo.

items.texto: Under the circumstances, your counteroffer seems fair, although I would like to propose one small change to the delivery date.

traduccion.es: Dadas las circunstancias, su contraoferta me parece justa, aunque me gustaría proponer un pequeño cambio en la fecha de entrega.

nota.es: Under the circumstances reconoce el contexto antes de matizar; although introduce el único cambio que pides.

items.texto: We accept your counteroffer in full, so please consider the matter closed and confirm the refund in writing.

traduccion.es: Aceptamos su contraoferta por completo, así que considere el asunto cerrado y confirme el reembolso por escrito.

nota.es: In full significa «por completo»: aceptas todos los términos. Después se pide confirmación por escrito.

objetivo.es: Distinguir en un texto de estudio la afirmación (claim), la prueba (evidence) y la opinión, juzgar si una prueba es sólida o solo anecdótica y reconocer las expresiones que señalan cada función.

A claim is an idea the writer defends, and it stays weak until the writer can back up the claim with evidence.
According to a survey of 300 students, most of them sleep under seven hours, which is the kind of data that supports the claim.
Some experts argue that teenagers need more sleep, but what they argue is a claim, not a fact, until it has been tested.
In my opinion, mornings are far too early for teenagers, but an opinion says what someone feels and cannot be checked like a fact.
A single story about one tired student is anecdotal, so it cannot back up a general claim the way a large survey can.
Writers who assert a sweeping claim, such as «all teenagers are lazy», should name a credible source, because a confident tone is not evidence.
Evidence: it gives a source and a figure that can be checked.
Claim: it states the main idea that the writer wants to defend.
Opinion: it says how the writer feels about early mornings.
Schools should start at nine. According to a survey of 300 students, 68 percent sleep under seven hours on school nights.

In this week's study skills podcast, the host reads out a short argument. Schools, she says, should start later in the morning. To back up that claim, she quotes a survey of three hundred students, most of whom slept under seven hours on school nights. texto.es: En un texto de estudio no todas las oraciones hacen el mismo trabajo. La afirmación (claim) es la idea que se defiende. La prueba (evidence) la respalda con datos, cifras o una fuente fiable: according to a survey…, the data show that… La opinión dice lo que alguien siente o cree y no se puede comprobar: in my opinion…, I feel that… Una anécdota (un solo caso) ilustra, pero no demuestra. En C1 no basta con entender el sentido: hay que reconocer la función de cada oración y cuánto pesa.

texto.es: En el lenguaje académico evitas decir «esto es así» cuando los datos solo apuntan en una dirección. Se matiza de tres formas: verbos (suggest, indicate, appear to, tend to), modales (may, might, could) y expresiones (to a certain extent, it could be argued that, there is limited evidence that). Matizar no es dudar: es decir exactamente hasta dónde llegan tus pruebas. Hay dos errores opuestos: exagerar (proves, all, always) y apilar tantos matices (perhaps it may possibly…) que nadie entiende qué afirmas. Suelen bastar uno o dos recursos por idea.

texto.es: Un resumen académico (abstract) cuenta un estudio completo en pocas líneas y casi siempre sigue el mismo orden: objetivo (aim: por qué se hizo), método (method: a quién y cómo), resultados y conclusión (qué encontraron y con qué cautela). Para localizar cada parte busca señales: The aim of this study is to…, The sample included…, The authors conclude that… La conclusión suele venir matizada (may suggest, is likely to) y, a veces, con una limitación que conviene leer entre líneas: una correlación no prueba una causa, y una muestra pequeña o voluntaria limita a quién se aplican los resultados.

A good paragraph opens with a clear claim and supports it with concrete evidence, such as a substantial difference in scores, before it ends with a cautious conclusion.

A good paragraph about study habits might begin like this: short daily study sessions may be more effective than one long night of cramming. A survey of two hundred students found that those who reviewed their notes regularly scored ten percent higher in the final exam. This suggests that regular review helps students retain information, although the effect may depend on the subject. To a certain extent, then, a steady schedule matters more than the number of hours.

Many students believe that one long night of study is the best way to prepare for an exam, but research suggests that regular short sessions may be more effective. A survey of 200 college students found that those who studied for forty minutes every day scored ten percent higher than those who studied only before the exam. This appears to show that regular review helps students retain information, although the effect may depend on the subject. For example, languages seem to benefit more from daily practice than essay subjects do. It could be argued that students who study every day are simply more interested in their courses, so the results should be read with care. To a certain extent, a good schedule matters more than the number of hours. In the long run, a short session every day is likely to be a better habit than cramming, but more research is needed.

texto.es: Un párrafo académico cauteloso tiene tres partes: una afirmación clara, la evidencia que la apoya (una cifra, una encuesta, un estudio) y una conclusión matizada. Usa al menos tres recursos de cautela de tipos distintos: un verbo (suggest, seem), un modal (may, might) y una expresión (to a certain extent, it could be argued that). No pongas cautela en todo: si tienes una cifra concreta, dila sin rodeos y reserva el matiz para la interpretación de esa cifra. Termina con una limitación o con una petición de más investigación.

items.respuesta: Many students believe that one long night of study is the best way to prepare for an exam, but research suggests that regular short sessions may be more effective. A survey of 200 college students found that those who studied for forty minutes every day scored ten percent higher than those who studied only before the exam. This appears to show that regular review helps students retain information, although the effect may depend on the subject. For example, languages seem to benefit more from daily practice than essay subjects do. It could be argued that students who study every day are simply more interested in their courses, so the results should be read with care. To a certain extent, a good schedule matters more than the number of hours. In the long run, a short session every day is likely to be a better habit than cramming, but more research is needed.

Some people think that listening to music while studying improves concentration. However, a study of 120 teenagers suggests that silence may be better for difficult tasks. The teenagers who worked in a quiet room scored eight percent higher on a reading test than those who listened to music. This seems to indicate that music can distract students, although it might help with simple tasks such as copying notes. It could be argued that some students are used to music and feel calmer with it, so the effect may depend on the person. Largely for this reason, the results should be read with care. Nevertheless, there is some evidence that a quiet schedule with short sessions is likely to work better for most students, but the sample was small and more research is needed before we can be sure of it.

texto.es: Presentar hallazgos a un grupo tiene tres movimientos: resumir el estudio con fidelidad (qué se hizo y qué se encontró, sin añadir ni exagerar), dar una conclusión cautelosa (the findings suggest…) y responder a las objeciones sin ponerte a la defensiva. Para responder, reconoce lo razonable (That is a fair point), admite la limitación (One limitation is that…) y mantén tu conclusión con matiz (Nevertheless, the results are likely to be valid). Reconocer un límite no debilita tu argumento: lo hace más creíble.

texto.es: Una charla se sigue mejor cuando el orador «señala el camino» (to signpost). Hay tres momentos: la apertura (Today I will present…, I will outline…, firstly…), las transiciones (Let's move on to…, Now I'd like to turn to…, I'll touch on… only briefly) y el cierre (To sum up…, Finally…). Si te desvías, dilo (If I may digress for a moment…) y vuelve al hilo. En C1 elige la fórmula que encaja con el momento y evita calcos como «pass to the next point».

items.texto: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming: today I will present the results of our neighbourhood survey, which reached more than six hundred households.

traduccion.es: Buenos días a todos y gracias por venir: hoy presentaré los resultados de nuestra encuesta del barrio, que llegó a más de seiscientos hogares.

nota.es: Apertura: saludo + agradecimiento + I will present… anuncia el tema y un dato sitúa al público.

items.texto: I will outline the talk in three parts, and firstly I will explain how we collected the data, before I turn to what residents told us.

nota.es: Let's move on to + parte es la transición habitual; touch on = tratar algo por encima, sin detenerse.

items.texto: Good speakers signpost every stage of a talk, and if they digress, they say so openly and return to the main point.

texto.es: Para describir un gráfico combina tres piezas: un verbo o sustantivo de tendencia (rise, fall, drop, fluctuate, plummet, level off, remain steady), un adverbio o adjetivo de intensidad (sharply, slightly, gradually; a steady rise) y una aproximación (roughly, around, just under, just over). Los cambios se completan con from… to… (partida y llegada) o con by (cuánto cambió); para proporciones usa account for. En C1 no basta con describir: si los datos son irregulares, evita hablar de «tendencia».

nota.es: sujeto: lo que se mide

punto de partida y de llegada

items.texto: Bus use rose sharply in March, from roughly 2,000 to 3,500 passengers, before it began to level off at the end of spring.

nota.es: Rose sharply: verbo de subida + adverbio de intensidad; from… to… da el punto de partida y de llegada; level off = dejar de subir y estabilizarse.

items.texto: The number of cyclists fell slightly between May and June, although the figure for the whole year was still higher than last year.

traduccion.es: El número de ciclistas bajó ligeramente entre mayo y junio, aunque la cifra de todo el año seguía siendo mayor que la del año pasado.

nota.es: Slightly describe un cambio pequeño; figure es la cifra o dato numérico; although introduce un contraste.

items.texto: Train use grew gradually over the year, and there was a steady rise in tram passengers, from 900 to just over 1,200.

traduccion.es: El uso del tren creció poco a poco durante el año, y hubo una subida constante de pasajeros de tranvía, de 900 a algo más de 1.200.

nota.es: Gradually: cambio lento; a steady rise: sustantivo de tendencia + adjetivo; just over = algo más de.

items.texto: Taxi use tends to fluctuate during the summer, and it can plummet when prices go up by almost twenty percent.

traduccion.es: El uso del taxi tiende a fluctuar durante el verano y puede caer en picado cuando los precios suben casi un veinte por ciento.

nota.es: Fluctuate: sube y baja sin rumbo claro; plummet: caída muy brusca; by + cifra indica cuánto cambia algo.

items.texto: Commuters account for roughly forty percent of all passengers, while tourists account for only about ten percent.

traduccion.es: Los viajeros habituales representan aproximadamente el cuarenta por ciento de los pasajeros, mientras que los turistas solo representan un diez por ciento.

nota.es: Account for + porcentaje: la parte que un grupo representa del total; roughly y about aproximan.

items.texto: The figure for taxis should remain steady at around 500 a day, unless the drop in tourist numbers continues.

traduccion.es: La cifra de taxis debería mantenerse estable en torno a 500 al día, a menos que continúe la caída del número de turistas.

nota.es: Remain steady: no cambia; drop es la caída como sustantivo y va seguida de in o of + lo que se mide.

titulo.es: Seguir la estructura de una charla

texto.es: Seguir una charla en audio es más fácil si sabes qué esperar: apertura (quién habla y cuántos puntos anuncia), puntos principales y cierre (resumen y takeaway). Anota solo palabras clave, no frases. Las señales te dicen dónde estás: «I will cover three main points» anuncia el esquema, «The second key point is…» abre el punto dos y «To recap…» avisa del cierre. Un desvío (a tangent) no es un punto nuevo: espera la señal de regreso. Además, el orador puede dar su opinión entre líneas: escucha también qué destaca.

Good morning, everyone. My topic today is our school book club, and I will cover three points: how it started, how it has grown and what we plan to do next. Firstly, let me explain how it started. Two years ago, only twelve students came to the first meeting, and we sat in the corridor because we had no room. Now let's move on to the second point: how the club has grown. As you can see in my chart, membership rose steadily, from twelve to thirty in two years. Roughly half of the members are first-year students, and just under a third are boys. Finally, I would like to turn to our plan. We would like to organise a reading night in June and invite two other schools. To sum up, the club started small, grew gradually and is ready for a new challenge. The message I want you to take home is simple: a few friends and a corridor were enough. Thank you for listening. I am happy to answer any questions.

titulo.es: El guion de una charla breve

texto.es: Un guion de dos minutos sigue la estructura que ya conoces: apertura (saludo, tema y número de partes), desarrollo con señalizadores (Firstly, Now let's move on to…) y cierre (To sum up… y una invitación a preguntas). Incluye una tendencia con cifras y aproximaciones (rose from 12 to 30; roughly half) y escribe frases cortas, pensadas para decirse en voz alta. En C1, cada parte cumple una función: la apertura crea conexión, la tendencia aporta pruebas y el cierre deja un mensaje claro.

items.respuesta: Good morning, everyone. My topic today is our school book club, and I will cover three points: how it started, how it has grown and what we plan to do next. Firstly, let me explain how it started. Two years ago, only twelve students came to the first meeting, and we sat in the corridor because we had no room. Now let's move on to the second point: how the club has grown. As you can see in my chart, membership rose steadily, from twelve to thirty in two years. Roughly half of the members are first-year students, and just under a third are boys. Finally, I would like to turn to our plan. We would like to organise a reading night in June and invite two other schools. To sum up, the club started small, grew gradually and is ready for a new challenge. The message I want you to take home is simple: a few friends and a corridor were enough. Thank you for listening. I am happy to answer any questions.

Hello, everyone, and welcome. Today I want to present my hobby, which is running, and I will outline the talk in three parts: why I started, how my training changed and my next goal. Firstly, I started running two years ago because I wanted to feel healthier. At the beginning, I could run for only ten minutes without stopping. Let's move on to the second part: my training. As you can see in my chart, my weekly distance rose gradually, from roughly five to around twenty kilometres in one year. I also take a short pause between exercises, and I keep a steady pace. Now I'd like to turn to my goal for next year. I hope to run a half marathon in the spring, and my friends will run with me. To sum up, running is cheap, simple and good for the head as well as for the body. Thank you very much for listening. Are there any questions?

To sum up my talk, I presented a study of 120 students who slept eight hours a night for a month. Their marks rose steadily, from 7.1 to 7.8, and the effect was clear for most of them. Now let me answer your two questions. First, you asked how many of the students were girls. texto.es: Responder preguntas difíciles sin perder el control requiere tres recursos. Si no entiendes, pide aclaración (Could you clarify…? Could you rephrase that?). Si no tienes el dato, sé honesto y matiza (Off the top of my head…; I'm afraid I don't have an accurate figure; I would need to check). Si alguien cuestiona tu conclusión, reconoce lo válido y mantén tu postura con cautela (That is a fair challenge. To a certain extent you are right, but… + una salvedad). Es mejor una respuesta honesta y matizada que inventar una cifra.

texto.es: Un mismo contenido cambia de sentido según tres cosas. El tono es la actitud del mensaje (cordial, brusco, sarcástico). El registro es el nivel de formalidad: no hablas igual con un amigo que con tu directora. Lo implícito es lo que se sugiere sin decirlo: una indirecta describe un hecho pero pide una acción. Cuando las palabras y la situación no encajan (un elogio tras un fallo), no lo tomes al pie de la letra: busca pistas en las palabras (please, grateful, hey), en las estructuras (would, could) y en el contexto.

texto.es: Este repaso junta cinco formas. Tag: el auxiliar contrario al final (You forgot it, didn't you?). Deducción: must have + participio si estás casi seguro y can't have si es imposible. Wish: pasado simple para el presente, had + participio para el pasado y would para quejas. Énfasis: It was Tom who… o What I need is… Cautela: may indicate, it could be argued that, no conclusive evidence. En español usamos el subjuntivo; en inglés cambia el tiempo verbal. En C1 cada forma comunica una postura: reproche, certeza, lamento, énfasis o prudencia.

This lyric is about the bus ride home at night, and its bittersweet mood comes from the contrast between the warm lights and the long, empty streets.
The theme is comfort: the singer wants to feel safe at home, although an undertone of tiredness suggests how long the day has been.
Each verse adds a detail about the journey, and the chorus repeats “take me home”, which makes that wish the emotional centre of the song.
“The city is a sleeping giant” is a metaphor, because it says that one thing is another without using like or as.
“Like a paper boat on a slow, warm river” is a simile, and its tender image makes the singer sound small but calm.
The streetlamps whisper advice to the traveller, so the lyric uses personification to make the night sound friendly rather than frightening.

Waiting for a friend who is very late.

texto.es: Para analizar una letra responde tres preguntas. ¿De qué trata? El tema es la idea central. ¿Cómo suena? El tono es la actitud o el ambiente (calm, tender, bittersweet), y a veces hay un matiz (undertone) que se siente debajo de las palabras. ¿Qué recursos usa y qué efecto tienen? Un símil compara con like o as; una metáfora dice que una cosa es otra; una personificación da acciones humanas a un objeto. El estribillo se repite para subrayar la idea y cada estrofa añade un detalle. Apoya siempre tu respuesta en una línea de la letra.

texto.es: En un relato combinas tiempos. El pasado simple cuenta las acciones puntuales (I opened the door), el pasado continuo pinta el escenario o lo que estaba pasando (It was raining) y el pasado perfecto marca lo que ocurrió antes (the train had left). El narrador en primera persona dice I. Para dar atmósfera añade un símil (like a wall), un detalle sensorial (the smell of rain) y una pista que anticipe lo que viene (foreshadow). Para destacar algo usa What I remember most is… o It was… who/that… En español usamos el imperfecto y el pluscuamperfecto; en inglés hay que elegir el tiempo con cuidado.

She has probably been waiting for you.” I called, and Sara answered at once. She was not angry. In fact, she had missed the train too, and she was waiting at the next station. We met her an hour later, and we laughed about the whole night. I will never forget how kind both of them were.

It was getting dark when I arrived at the cinema, and a long line was waiting outside. I had bought the tickets two days before, but when I looked in my bag, I understood that I had left them at home. My heart was beating like a drum. What I felt most was shame, because Leo had already told everyone that the film was his idea. I walked to the desk and explained the problem. The woman smiled and said, “Do not worry. Show me the message on your phone.” I looked for it, but my hands were shaking. Finally I found it. It was a small miracle that the message was still there! titulo.es: Las cuatro jugadas de una reunión

texto.es: En una reunión cortés se encadenan cuatro jugadas. Primero, una propuesta clara (I'd like to propose a compromise…; What if we…?). Segundo, una concesión: reconoces un punto del otro (Admittedly…; I take your point). Tercero, una discrepancia con tacto: no dices «estás equivocado», sino With respect, I see it differently o I'd like to voice a concern. Por último, un acuerdo concreto con plazo (Shall we agree to try it for a month?). Así se evita el deadlock y se llega a un consenso. Suaviza con perhaps o a bit, y cierra con To sum up.

My thesis is that every cycling lane in the city centre should be physically separated from traffic, not merely painted on the road.
Protected routes may encourage hesitant families to cycle, but the writer presents that outcome as a likelihood rather than a promise, and she is right to hedge.
Surely no sensible parent would send a child cycling beside heavy lorries? The writer treats the answer as obvious, and that is how a rhetorical question works.
Critics say that the scheme is too costly, so a fair writer will concede a point before she tries to make a case for the plan as a whole.
A sweeping statement such as everybody hates cycling may sound firm, but a single exception is enough to undermine it.
Writers who deserve our trust back up their claims with evidence, whereas those who only want to persuade us often rely on emotion.

Museums should stay free only for children, because adults can afford the price.
Museums should raise their entrance fee, because galleries are short of money.

Museums should be free for everyone. I will argue that an entrance fee quietly shuts out the very people who would benefit most from a visit. Critics claim that free entry would leave galleries short of money, and I concede that point: somebody has to pay for the roof. Nevertheless, when the capital opened its main museum without charge, visits doubled within a year, and donations rose as well. Surely a country that is proud of its past should let every child see it? Free entry may not solve every problem, but the evidence suggests that it is a sound choice, and it deserves the council's attention.

Remote work is not the threat that some managers imagine. Critics argue that employees who stay at home are less productive, and I admit that a few may well be. Surely a firm that cares about results should welcome that? I am not saying that the office is useless; teams probably benefit from meeting regularly. texto.es: Analizar un texto de opinión es buscar tres cosas. La tesis es lo que el autor defiende y suele aparecer pronto (My thesis is…; I will argue that…). El tono es su actitud: firme, molesto, prudente, justo. Los recursos son los medios con los que convence: datos que respaldan la idea, una pregunta retórica (Surely…?), una concesión a los críticos (concede a point) y la cautela (hedge) con may, seems o to some extent. Cita siempre la frase que lo demuestra: un buen análisis no dice «es firme», dice «es firme porque…».

nota.es: tesis: lo que el autor defiende

formula.texto: Critics say…; I concede that point.

nota.es: concesión: reconoce la objeción

filas.texto: Hace que el autor suene justo

items.texto: My thesis is that every cycling lane in the city centre should be physically separated from traffic, not merely painted on the road.

traduccion.es: Mi tesis es que cada carril para bicicletas del centro debería estar separado físicamente del tráfico, y no solo pintado en la calzada.

nota.es: La tesis es lo que el autor defiende y suele aparecer pronto: My thesis is… / I will argue that…

items.texto: Protected routes may encourage hesitant families to cycle, but the writer presents that outcome as a likelihood rather than a promise, and she is right to hedge.

traduccion.es: Las rutas protegidas pueden animar a familias dudosas a ir en bici, pero la autora presenta ese resultado como una probabilidad y no como una promesa, y hace bien en matizar.

nota.es: May es un recurso de cautela: hedge es suavizar una afirmación que no puedes probar del todo.

items.texto: Surely no sensible parent would send a child cycling beside heavy lorries? The writer treats the answer as obvious, and that is how a rhetorical question works.

traduccion.es: ¿Acaso algún padre sensato mandaría a un niño en bici junto a camiones pesados? La autora da la respuesta por obvia, y así funciona una pregunta retórica.

nota.es: Surely…? no espera respuesta: presenta la idea del autor como evidente y empuja al lector a estar de acuerdo.

items.texto: Critics say that the scheme is too costly, so a fair writer will concede a point before she tries to make a case for the plan as a whole.

traduccion.es: Los críticos dicen que el plan es demasiado costoso, así que un autor justo concederá un punto antes de intentar defender el plan en su conjunto.

nota.es: Conceder un punto (concede a point) no debilita la tesis: al contrario, hace que el autor suene justo.

items.texto: A sweeping statement such as everybody hates cycling may sound firm, but a single exception is enough to undermine it.

traduccion.es: Una generalización excesiva como «todo el mundo odia ir en bici» puede sonar firme, pero basta una sola excepción para debilitarla.

nota.es: Firm describe el tono; una sweeping statement (con everybody, nobody, always) es un punto débil de un texto.

items.texto: Writers who deserve our trust back up their claims with evidence, whereas those who only want to persuade us often rely on emotion.

traduccion.es: Los autores que merecen nuestra confianza respaldan sus afirmaciones con pruebas, mientras que los que solo quieren convencernos suelen apoyarse en la emoción.

nota.es: Back up = respaldar con pruebas; persuade = convencer, a menudo con emoción además de datos.

consigna.es: Lee el texto y elige cuál es la tesis de la autora.

feedback.es: La tesis aparece tras «I will argue that»: una entrada de pago deja fuera a quienes más ganarían con la visita. Las otras opciones cambian el alcance o recogen la postura de los críticos.

pista.es: La tesis suele anunciarse con una fórmula como «I will argue that».

opciones: Museums should charge no entrance fee, because fees keep out those who benefit most.
Museums should stay free only for children, because adults can afford the price.
Museums should raise their entrance fee, because galleries are short of money.
items.texto: Museums should be free for everyone. I will argue that an entrance fee quietly shuts out the very people who would benefit most from a visit. Critics claim that free entry would leave galleries short of money, and I concede that point: somebody has to pay for the roof. Nevertheless, when the capital opened its main museum without charge, visits doubled within a year, and donations rose as well. Surely a country that is proud of its past should let every child see it? Free entry may not solve every problem, but the evidence suggests that it is a sound choice, and it deserves the council's attention.

feedback.es: Es una pregunta retórica: no espera respuesta ni pide al lector que valore las pruebas; da por obvia la tesis y empuja al lector a coincidir con ella.

pista.es: Fíjate en que nadie necesita contestar la pregunta: la respuesta ya está dada.

I am not saying that every road needs a concrete wall, and I accept that the cost is real. But surely a child on a bicycle deserves more than a white line? If councils want more people to cycle, they must first make it feel safe.

items.texto: Remote work is not the threat that some managers imagine. Critics argue that employees who stay at home are less productive, and I admit that a few may well be. Yet the largest study on the subject, covering some ten thousand workers, found that work stayed just as good, while far fewer people quit their jobs. Surely a firm that cares about results should welcome that? I am not saying that the office is useless; teams probably benefit from meeting regularly. Even so, insisting on five days a week seems to me a habit rather than a strategy, and it may cost companies their best people.

consigna.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe «I am not saying that the office is useless»?

feedback.es: Se adelanta a una objeción («entonces, ¿la oficina no sirve?») y limita su tesis para que siga siendo creíble; no retrocede en ella ni busca tranquilizar a los jefes sobre el rendimiento.

opciones: To step back from his thesis and accept that offices are still necessary.
To reassure managers that employees will still work well from home.
To deal with an objection early and keep his argument fair.

titulo.es: Editar un borrador en tres pasadas

texto.es: Editar es revisar un borrador en tres pasadas. Formas: concordancia, tiempos y artículos. Registro: en un texto formal quita la jerga y las contracciones y suaviza (tone down) lo demasiado coloquial. Conectores: although y whereas van dentro de la oración y no admiten but; however y therefore unen dos oraciones y piden punto y coma antes y coma después, porque una coma sola crea un comma splice. En español decimos «aunque… pero»; en inglés se elige uno solo. Anota por qué cambias cada cosa y termina leyendo en voz alta (proofread).

traduccion.es: La prueba tuvo éxito; sin embargo, la muestra era pequeña, y mi primer borrador, con una coma en lugar de un punto y coma antes de however, era un comma splice.

nota.es: However une dos oraciones: punto y coma antes y coma después. Con una coma sola se produce un comma splice.

traduccion.es: Los precios del combustible subieron bruscamente; por lo tanto, muchos hogares gastaron menos, mientras que las familias más ricas casi no notaron la diferencia.

nota.es: Therefore introduce la consecuencia con la misma puntuación que however; whereas contrasta dos grupos dentro de una oración.

items.texto: A casual message to a colleague sounds friendly, but the same wording may seem careless in a report, so reword it carefully.

traduccion.es: Un mensaje informal a un colega suena amistoso, pero las mismas palabras pueden parecer descuidadas en un informe, así que reformúlalo con cuidado.

nota.es: Casual describe el registro informal; reword es decir lo mismo con otras palabras, más adecuadas al lector.

items.texto: When you proofread your final draft, look for every sentence fragment, because a group of words without a main verb often passes for a full sentence.

traduccion.es: Cuando revises tu borrador final, busca cada fragmento de oración, porque un grupo de palabras sin verbo principal suele parecer una oración completa a simple vista.

nota.es: Proofread es la última lectura, centrada en errores pequeños; un sentence fragment es un trozo de frase que se presenta como si fuera una oración.

I firmly believe that public transport in our city should be free for everyone. First, it would help families who spend a large part of their income on travel, and it would encourage more people to leave their cars at home. As a result, the streets would be quieter, the air would be cleaner and the centre would be safer for children. It is true that free buses would cost the council a great deal of money, and some critics argue that the service might become crowded. To some extent, I share that worry. However, it seems that the money could come from parking fees and from the money that we already spend on roads. Perhaps we could begin with a one-year trial and review the results carefully. On the other hand, nobody can promise that every passenger would leave a car at home. Even so, on balance, I would say that the benefits outweigh the costs, and I stand by that view. In short, free public transport would make our city fairer, cleaner and calmer.

texto.es: En una intervención de un minuto tienes cuatro movimientos. Postura: dila con firmeza (I firmly believe…). Concesión: reconoce un punto contrario (It is true that…; Admittedly…). Matiz: suaviza lo que no puedes probar (to some extent, may, on balance). Cierre: resume en una frase (In short…). Bajo presión debes pensar sobre la marcha (think on your feet): gana tiempo (buy time) con Let me think about that y mantén tu postura (stand by your view). Evita usar dos fórmulas a la vez: no se dice I am agree ni in my opinion, for me.

nota.es: postura: firme y en primera persona
concesión: reconoces y defiendes
matiz: no lo afirmas del todo
cierre: resumen en una frase

items.respuesta: I firmly believe that public transport in our city should be free for everyone. First, it would help families who spend a large part of their income on travel, and it would encourage more people to leave their cars at home. As a result, the streets would be quieter, the air would be cleaner and the centre would be safer for children. It is true that free buses would cost the council a great deal of money, and some critics argue that the service might become crowded. To some extent, I share that worry. However, it seems that the money could come from parking fees and from the money that we already spend on roads. Perhaps we could begin with a one-year trial and review the results carefully. On the other hand, nobody can promise that every passenger would leave a car at home. Even so, on balance, I would say that the benefits outweigh the costs, and I stand by that view. In short, free public transport would make our city fairer, cleaner and calmer.

However, it seems that the money could come from parking fees and from the money that we already spend on roads. Perhaps we could begin with a one-year trial and review the results carefully. On the other hand, nobody can promise that every passenger would leave a car at home. Even so, on balance, I would say that the benefits outweigh the costs, and I stand by that view. In short, free public transport would make our city fairer, cleaner and calmer.

My position is clear: public transport should cost nothing for residents. Admittedly, it is not a cheap idea, and the council would have to find a large sum every year. Even so, I am convinced that the money would be well spent. Cheaper travel would help students, workers and older people who cannot afford a car, and it may also reduce traffic in the centre. Some say that buses would become crowded, and I agree that the service would need more vehicles. Perhaps the city could add a few routes at busy hours and review the plan after twelve months. It seems to me that nobody can be certain of the result before trying. However, doing nothing is also a choice, and it has costs of its own: noise, pollution and long delays. To sum up, free transport is a fair and sensible idea, and on balance I think it is worth a try.

titulo.es: El caso final: interpretar, responder, defender

texto.es: Este cierre junta todo el nivel en un caso de tres pasos. Interpretar: lee el mensaje buscando tono, registro y lo implícito (read between the lines; her email implied that…). Responder con tacto: agradece, reconoce un punto (I understand…; I admit…) y rechaza o propón con suavidad (I'm afraid…; nevertheless, I must decline). Defender tu postura con matiz: firmeza (I firmly believe…), concesión y cautela (may, to some extent), buscando el equilibrio (strike a balance, tread a fine line) entre ser sincero y ser cortés, sin ceder en lo esencial (hold your ground). Cierra con un acuerdo concreto (Could we agree to…?).

items.texto: When I read the landlord's message twice, I began to interpret the polite wording as a gentle complaint about the state of the garden.

items.texto: Her email never said that I was late, but it implied that I should have arrived earlier, so I had to read between the lines.

nota.es: Imply + that + oración: sugerir sin decirlo; no se dice implied me. Read between the lines: captar lo no dicho.

items.texto: I have to tread a fine line here: I admit that the landlord's costs have risen, although I take issue with the claim that the rent rise is unavoidable.

nota.es: Tread a fine line: equilibrio delicado entre firmeza y cortesía; admit reconoce un punto débil, y take issue with discrepa con educación.

items.texto: Writing with tact means you strike a balance between honesty and courtesy, and a little nuance shows that you have weighed both sides.
